name: Brow shaving / brow reshaping for tilt

lead: Looksmaxxers reshape or trim their brows to make the eye area look more upward-angled, aiming for a positive tilt and a 'hunter eyes' look. The change is visible as soon as the hair is cut, and it costs almost nothing.

Changing the brow's outline changes the line the eye reads against, which proponents say alters the apparent angle of the eye. No studies were found testing whether trimming changes perceived tilt; the published research is on surgical brow shaping and lifting.

paras: People remove or trim hair with tweezers, wax, thread, scissors or a razor, and some redraw the shape with brow makeup. Because hair regrows, the shape is maintained with regular grooming, and many try small changes first.

Hair generally regrows, so changes are temporary, though over-trimming or over-plucking can leave gaps that take time to fill back in. Surgical brow shaping carries standard operative risks and is a separate matter from grooming.

angle.text: Trimming or reshaping the brows changes the line above the eye, which looksmaxxers use to make the eye area look more upward-tilted and 'hunter'-like. The change is cheap, reversible and visible right away. Its effect on perceived tilt has not been studied.

lead: Brow reshaping for tilt refers to trimming, shaving or otherwise altering the eyebrows to change how the eye area appears angled, a concern in looksmaxxing discussions of positive canthal tilt and the 'hunter eyes' look. In everyday grooming this is done by removing or trimming hair; Wikipedia lists tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming as common methods, and notes that some people shave the brows and draw them on [1].

Published research on the topic is surgical rather than cosmetic grooming. Plastic surgeons have described procedures that reshape brow position, including transcutaneous brow shaping and gliding brow lifts, in which the relationship between the medial and lateral portions of the brow is emphasised over overall height [2][3]. No studies of brow shaving or trimming for perceived eye tilt were found.
infobox: Transcutaneous brow shaping, gliding brow lift [2][3]
Hair regrows; surgery is not readily reversible

paras: Eyebrows are reported to protect the eye from sweat and debris and to be important in communicating emotion [1]. Brow shape has varied across cultures and eras, from high-painted brows in 8th-century Japan to thin brows in the 1920s and 1930s [1]. In appearance communities, brow shape is discussed as one factor in the impression of tilt, since an upward-slanting lateral brow can alter how the eye region reads.

Common grooming methods include tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming with small scissors, with permanent tinting and cosmetics also used to define the brows [1]. Brow hair that is removed can grow back, though repeated removal is not examined in the sources reviewed here.

Surgeons authoring a 2017 paper argued that the relationship between the lateral and medial brow is aesthetically more important than absolute height, and described transcutaneous brow shaping as a way to shape the brow precisely and correct minor asymmetry [2]. A 2025 study described an endoscopic gliding forehead lift designed to lift both medial and lateral brow in Asian patients [3]. A 2022 review noted that no work has defined an ideal male eye and brow comparable to that for women [4].
No studies found on brow shaving or trimming for tilt. Related published work concerns surgical brow shaping and lifting, summarised above [2][3][4].
